messages.author: 181bcebaf89c73b8
messages.subject: eigenvectors_sym and eigenvalues_sym
parts:
Sorry if this is documented somewhere, but if I do both
eigenvectors_sym and eigenvalues_sym on the same symmetric matrix is
the eigendecomposition calculated twice or is Stan smart enough to
realize it can compute both simultaneously?

Thanks

David.

--
David A. Knowles,
Stanford University.
E-mail: know...@gmail.com
Web: http://cs.stanford.edu/~davidknowles/

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] eigenvectors_sym and eigenvalues_sym
parts:
We really need to either hack a return type or wait until we have tuples. We will eventually be adding a type that would look something like:

tuple<vector, matrix> eigendecomse(matrix x);

Like an R list, only typed. But that's a ways off unless Sean or Mitzi tackle it because I'm diving into higher-order autodiff next.

- Bob

messages.author: 3d7541308bd2e290
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] eigenvectors_sym and eigenvalues_sym
parts: >> tuple<vector, matrix> eigendecomse(matrix x);

That would be reaaallly handy.

For what it's worth, it looks like the eigensolver in Stan spits out normalized eigenvectors (specified up to the sign), so you can get the eigenvalues you need with v' A v for now (if you need the eigenvectors too). A little annoying, but less annoying than computing things twice haha.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] eigenvectors_sym and eigenvalues_sym
parts:
I think the bigger deal is that we haven't written
analytic derivatives for eigendecompositions, so they're
memory hogs and potentially slower than they would be
with analytic derivatives. We have a long way to go to
get all of our analytic derivatives in place for matrix ops.
Anyone who knows this stuff and can help, it'd be most
appreciated!

- Bob

for the SoftAbs metric.  See https://arxiv.org/pdf/1212.4693.pdf
Section IIB, and the references therein.  They are super
weird, though.
